title: How Many Dragons to BEAT My Chess Bot?
summary: 'How many dragons to beat my chess bot': the creator plays his own site bot Tony (≈2100, Fairy-Stockfish limited to 2100) with only a king plus N dragons (dragon = bishop + knight) against Tony's full army, adding one dragon after each loss ('Add 1 Dragon' button on iwantcheckmate.com). Strategy: dragon batteries on f7/c7, sacrifice-and-recapture mating patterns from the Grandmaster video. Lost with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 dragons; won with 6 dragons, becoming the first entry on the site's stats ('One player has now defeated my bot with six dragons').
rules: Player white: Ke1 + N dragons; Tony black: full standard army (castling kq).
Dragon (archbishop) = moves like a bishop or a knight.
Dragon placement order on site: d1, f1, c1, g1, b1, h1, a1, e2, d2, f2, c2, g2, b2, h2, a2 (N=1..15).
Start N=1; each loss or draw: 'Add 1 Dragon' (N+1); max 15 then 'You Ran Out of Dragons!'.
Opponent: Tony (2100) = Fairy-Stockfish variant 'dragonchallenge', UCI_LimitStrength, UCI_Elo 2100.
win_condition: Checkmate Tony with as few dragons as possible. Video: won with 6 dragons.
